position_suggestion.basis: No sizing action -- this is the daily advisor check-in, not a new pick. UBER is already far above the 25% concentration guideline.
position_suggestion.concentration_note: UBER is ~79.4% of NAV, more than 3x the 25% single-name guideline; any further addition is out of the question regardless of thesis strength.

advisor_questions.framing: Holding decision -- whether to keep, trim, or add to the book's dominant position, not a trade.
questions: This position is now ~79% of NAV -- did it get there through a deliberate conviction-sizing decision, or through price appreciation and drift from a smaller original stake, and would you choose to put 79% of new money into UBER today at $71.40?

With Tesla's Cybercab, Waymo's robotaxi expansion, and Uber's own AV-partner strategy (NVIDIA, Zoox, Wayve) all converging on the same market, does Uber's demand-aggregation moat survive a shift toward owned-fleet robotaxi economics, or does it erode as those partners' networks mature?

The DCF and consensus models imply 45-58% upside to fair value -- over a 5-10 year view, is that gap more likely to close through actual free-cash-flow growth, or does it rest on optimistic take-rate and AV-capex-payback assumptions that may not hold?

If the thesis is wrong -- margin compression from robotaxi competition, or an adverse outcome in the pending passenger-assault MDL bellwether trials -- how would you find out, and how quickly could a position this size actually be trimmed without moving the price against you?
advisor_questions.note: This is the mandated daily check-in on the book's largest position, independent of today's (flat) news flow.
